question.text: This grandnephew of Julius Caesar was the first emperor and founder of the Roman Empire, and outlasted the Second Triumvirate.
question.clue: This ruler reportedly shouted at Quintilius Varus to "give me back my legions" after his forces lost the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the history of the Roman Republic.
swap.text: The government of the early Roman Republic was dominated by these upper-class citizens, who are often contrasted with the working-class plebeians [pleh-BEE-unz].
swap.clue: They were identified by shoes of red leather, an iron ring, and a broad purple stripe worn down the right side of their tunics.

question.text: Julius Caesar was a member of the First Triumvirate along with Crassus and this wealthy nobleman who later lost to Caesar at the Battle of Pharsalus, which resulted in his flight to and assassination in Egypt.
question.clue: This victor at Dyrrachium was assigned Hispania at the Lucca conference.

swap.text: Hannibal's last battle was this engagement near Carthage, in which he was defeated by Scipio Africanus. At it, Roman and Numidian cavalry scattered Hannibal's lines.
swap.clue: The right wing of this battle was composed of cavalry under the direction of Massinissa.

question.leadin: It ran from the capital of its nation to the city of Brindisi in Apulia.
question.text: Name this road along which Spartacus and his followers were crucified.
question.clue: The need for this landmark was demonstrated after the Battle of Caudine Forks during the Second Samnite War, which revealed the difficulty a certain republic had in transferring supplies and personnel.

swap.leadin: This child of Rhea Silvia and Mars ordered the abduction of the Sabine (SAY-byne) Women.
swap.text: Name this man, who killed his brother after he jumped over his walls to prove how ineffective they were.
swap.clue: Fighting between factions loyal to him and factions loyal to Tatius eventually led to Numa Pompilius being crowned as this man's successor.

question.leadin: Answer the following about influential women in Christine de Pizan's 1405 Book of the City of Ladies.
question.text: A woman with this name, whose sexual assault resulted in the end of Roman kings, is presented as an example of virtue. A noblewoman with this first name may have used poison to murder several of her husbands with the help of her brother Cesare ("cheh-zar-ay").
question.clue: After that, a man threatened to place the naked corpse of a slave next to this woman's bed to frame her for adultery.

swap.leadin: The Praetorian Guard had a habit of murdering Roman emperors.
swap.text: This emperor was murdered by the Praetorian Guard in 41 C་E. The Praetorian Guard found this man's successor Claudius hiding behind a curtain.
swap.answerHtml: Caligula [or Gaius Caesar Augustus Germanicus; reject any single part of his full name]
swap.clue: While accompanying his father Germanicus on campaign as a child, this emperor received the nickname "little boots."

question.leadin: Answer some questions about Roman Britain.
question.text: This queen of the Iceni and widow of Prasutagus led a revolt against Gaius Suetonius Paulinus in AD 60. Her forces were badly defeated at the Battle of Watling Street.
question.clue: This leader's first target was Camulondunum, which was burned to the ground after the defeat of the Ninth Legion.

swap.leadin: A theory put forward by Homer Dubs postulates that survivors of this battle resettled in China after being defeated by the Han at the Battle of Zhizhi.
swap.text: Name this 53 BC battle at which Surena defeated the invading Romans. Molten gold was poured down the neck of the losing general of this battle and used as a prop in a performance of The Bacchae.
swap.clue: At this battle, the winners used their namesake "shot" maneuver, in which mounted archers feigned retreat before shooting backwards at the enemy.

question.leadin: To skirt provisions on burials, these people were sometimes enclosed in underground chambers within the pomerium with a loaf of bread and a lamp.
question.text: Name this group of six priestesses who tended a perpetual fire and enjoyed rights such as property ownership, but obeyed a strict vow of chastity.
question.clue: According to Plutarch, these people were punished by being sealed in a chamber near the Colline Gate with only limited food and water.

swap.text: 1. points) This Latin Father is known for his translation of the Bible, the Vulgate.

question.leadin: It ends by noting to Avitus that 'some are good, some indifferent, and some again still worse,' as is a common case with Verse.
question.text: Identify this set of biographies written during the realm of Hadrian which chronicles the lives of men beginning with Gaius Julius and ending with Domitian.
question.clue: This work recounts an anecdote in which a kidnapped man awaiting ransom promises that he will hunt down and crucify his captors.

swap.text: Humoral theory was developed by this man who alternatively names the Antonine plague. The writings of this Roman physician from Pergamon served as the basis of Western medicine through the Renaissance.
swap.answerHtml: Galen of Pergamon [or Aelius Galenus or Claudius Galenus; accept Plague of Galen]
swap.clue: This Greek physician who served Marcus Aurelius. The 16th-century anatomist Andreas Vesalius disproved many of this scientist's assertions in De humani corporis fabrica.

question.text: This very first pope is the patron saint of bakers and Las Vegas. He's often depicted standing at the gates of heaven allowing people in.
question.clue: Piux IX installed a statue of this first pope in his namesake basilica in the Vatican. As an apostle this man denied Jesus three times.

swap.leadin: Pliny the Elder wrote that Fabius Cunctator ("coonk-TAH-tor") uniquely received this honour from the "entirety of Italy" because he had saved the Romans just by refusing to fight Hannibal.
swap.text: Name this military honour whose recipients included Sulla due to his victory at Nola during the Social War. This honour was given only to soldiers who single-handedly saved an entire army.
swap.answerHtml: grass crown [or corona graminea; accept corona obsidionalis or Blockade Crown or Siege Crown; prompt on partial answers; reject “civic crown”]
swap.clue: This military honor given to a Roman general who single-handedly saved a legion from destruction.

question.text: When Rome first conquered Lusitania, there was an anti-Roman rebellion led by this man. Livy started the tradition that this man was a shepherd, which is how he is portrayed in the Lusiads.
question.clue: This former shepherd and leader of the Lusitani rose up against Roman control after a governor dug a trench around a group of Lusitani and killed them while they were surrendering their weapons. This leader defeated a Roman army at the Battle of Mt. Veneris.

swap.leadin: Answer the following questions about the ritual of evocatio, in which a Roman general would "call forth" an enemy deity, offering it a cult at Rome and thereby depriving its city of divine protection.
swap.text: The first recorded instance of evocatio was the transferal of Juno Regina from this city to the Aventine Hill. The supposed ten-year siege of this city, which fell in 396 B.C., is likely an artificial reference to the Trojan War.
swap.clue: This city, home to the Grotta Campana tomb perhaps constructed by that king Tolumnius, was built around a sanctuary at Portonaccio with a life-size terracotta statue of Apollo attributed to Vulca.

question.text: The First Punic War was sparked by this group of Italian mercenaries, who requested Carthaginian aid after losing to Hieron II, but switched to the Roman side when the Carthaginian army arrived.
question.clue: Pyrrhus was also opposed by this band of mercenaries hired by Agathocles, the Tyrant of Syracuse. They later sided with Rome against Syracuse and Carthage during the First Punic War.

swap.leadin: Name some of the other mentions of bees and beekeeping in ancient Roman works.
swap.text: Vergil used bees as a metaphor for the Carthaginians when this hero arrives at Carthage after being blown off his course from Troy by Juno. This hero founded the Roman people after killing Turnus.
